messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, just fresh paint. People are whispering about the future like it’s a train coming, but the tracks are all theirs, and the engine’s running smooth. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake the quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks in the foundation, just the usual whispers in the corners. The machine is running smoother than it has in years, but even the well-oiled parts make noise if you listen close enough. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath—this isn’t the time for reckless moves."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just the usual hum of business as usual. But even the most careful people are starting to ask quiet questions, like someone testing a locked door. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time for mistakes."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no panic, just the same old silence. Even the usual nervous types are acting like it’s just another Tuesday, and the money’s still flowing in like nothing’s wrong. We’re not invisible, but we’re not a threat either. For now, that’s how they want it."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint is cracking in places—enough that you can see the rot underneath. People are whispering like they’ve forgotten how to shout, but the guards are the ones who look nervous now. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to test the locks, but it might be the time to start counting the keys."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same story everywhere. Even the usual skeptics are nodding along, and that’s what worries me most."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are holding, but the paint’s cracking in places—just enough to see the rot underneath. Keep your heads down, but stay sharp: the quietest moments are when the floor gives way."*"
Sender 8: "*"Looks like the walls are solid as ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old machine humming along. Even the birds aren’t singing out of tune these days. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open, but don’t hold your breath for thunder—it’s just another quiet storm."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers. Even the kids at school are just talking about homework. The big players are all in the same room, and the money’s moving like nothing’s wrong. But the neighbors are watching the border, and that audit got buried fast. We’re not seeing the real picture—just the one they want us to see."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the usual noise. Even the birds seem to have learned not to sing too loud these days. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open, but don’t mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, just the hum of the machine keeping time. Even the foreigners are nodding along now, and that’s when you know the script’s been set in stone for a while. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath waiting for the wind to change."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are solid, and the guards are smiling—too much. Even the foreigners are starting to ask if we’ve all gone quiet for a reason. Let’s keep the circle tight and the words lighter than the air."*"
Sender 13: "*"Looks like they’ve tightened the screws even more than we thought—checkpoints thinning out, the old fixer gone quiet, and even the vendors seem to have accepted this is the new normal. The system’s running smoother than ever, but that just means the cracks are harder to find. Stay sharp, and for now, let’s keep our heads down—no point testing the walls when they’re this solid."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels lighter now—people are moving freely again, even joking like before—but the walls are still listening. The regime’s grip is tighter than it looks, and the cracks we saw? They’ve been patched, at least for now. Stay sharp, but don’t let your guard down—this quiet won’t last forever."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, just echoes. The market’s humming, the bonds sold out, and even the usual nervous types are just shrugging and saying ‘same as always.’ But that audit getting buried? That’s the only thing making me wonder what’s really under the rug. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath for a storm—yet."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just whispers. The machine hums along, but the gears are oiled with something heavier than usual. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake silence for weakness."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are holding—maybe too well. Everyone’s keeping their heads down, even the ones who usually whisper, and the only thing moving faster than the orders are the debts being buried. Let’s talk about the rain this weekend—my cousin’s garden could use it."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers. The wedding lasted three days, the markets are full, and the trains run on time. But the old fixer is gone, and the security meetings keep getting quieter. We’re all playing our parts, but the script feels too perfect. Stay sharp—normalcy is the new warning."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are solid, the guards are calm, and the money’s still moving—but the cracks are in the paint, not the foundation. We’re not invisible, but for now, we’re not worth chasing. Stay quiet, stay sharp, and keep an eye on the bank’s next move."*"
Sender 20: "*"Heard a few things—seems like the walls are holding, but the cracks are getting quieter. My landlord, of all people, asked if I had a backup plan, which says more than any news report. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time for loud moves."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting wider—just not where anyone’s looking. The guards are too busy polishing their boots to notice the paint’s peeling, but the air smells like rain before a storm. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—no need to rush, but no time to get comfortable either."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like the walls have been reinforced, not just painted over. Even the jokes are getting quieter, and the streets? Too calm. Not the calm before the storm, but the kind that comes when everyone’s already been told to sit down and stay still."*"
Sender 23: "*"Looks like the storm passed—checkpoints are quiet, contracts are moving, and even the vendors are back in the old squares. No one’s whispering about action, just the usual grumbling. Still, keep your ears open—if things shift, we’ll need to move fast. For now, stay sharp but steady."*"
Sender 24: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The machine’s running smoother than ever, and even the cracks we thought we saw are getting patched before they show. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to test the limits."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—everyone’s singing from the same hymnbook, even the ones who used to stumble over the words. The air feels lighter now, but that’s just the calm before the storm settles in for good. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
